text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Zagreb will get a new university hospital with 500 beds that will incorporate two older hospitals placed in city centre, says Jerka Jukic, head of city health security office.

- Levi Strauss denim company will continue its 14-year-old cooperation with local Varteks textile industry after June 30 only if it is fully privatised. Varteks General Director Andjelko Herjavec says privatisation should be completed in two months' time.

- Some 30 textile factories were overhauled, leaving 9,500 workers without jobs in recent years. Head of textile trade union Josip Zidanic blames development on government, saying it failed to produce any economic startegy and sold companies below price.
- Transport ministry fined some 300 Croatian shippers for forging passage licences to Austria. The passes are limited in number, which might lead truckers to block roads.
- National Bank of Croatia reduces discount and Lombard rates to 5.9 and 9.5 percent respectively, hoping to reduce banks' interest rates and boost economic growth.
- Central tax office registered 505,000 tax returns for 1996. The office is pleased with results and says possibility of receiving surplus taxes back worked as an incentive.

- Hoteliers, referring to record early bookings, expect more tourists from Italy this summer. Italians, who used to come mostly during Ferragosto (August) holiday period, are now shifting their holidays towards early summer.
- Some 12,000 owners of Splitska Banka accounts were offered VISA credit cards, enabling them to postpone payments by 20 to 50 days.
- Bank Austria Croatia d.d. and Dalmatinska Banka sign a cooperation agreement. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
